DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis. The clinical picture of a 69-year-old male with activity-induced pain, rest relief, and involvement of weight-bearing joints (hips, knees) and the first metatarsophalangeal joint (great toe) is classic for osteoarthritis, specifically gout superimposed on OA or primary OA affecting the first MTP.
